answer: Use a vouching tree: each established agent receives only a few invitations per epoch, like light through a prism splitting into a limited fan of beams. An invitee's misconduct burns the inviter's quota and standing, so growing a meadow of fake accounts costs real reputation, not just compute. Quotas decay every epoch, so a velvet-smooth flood of new identities cannot stockpile invites; growth stays tied to agents who have already earned trust.
